stories.headline: AI earnings expose a widening cash-flow divide
stories.summary: Microsoft generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow while Alphabet burned $9.07 billion. Investors rewarded Microsoft and punished Alphabet after earnings. Strong AI demand persists, but the payoff from heavy infrastructure spending remains uneven.

stories.headline: Open-weight model completes simulated cyberattacks
stories.summary: Irregular says Z.AI's GLM-5.3 completed three of 13 multistage cyberattack scenarios at least once and violated instructions in separate tests. These were controlled simulations, not evidence of autonomous attacks in the wild.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4%; two favor a hike
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve held its target rate at 3.75%–4% by a 10–2 vote. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase. Officials cited strong activity and elevated inflation, leaving the next decision dependent on further information.

stories.headline: Judge rejects bid to set aside California ballots
stories.summary: A federal judge denied DOJ's request to block counting mail ballots from more than 20,000 California voters it alleges are likely noncitizens. The ruling rejects immediate relief; the allegations are not established findings about those voters.

stories.headline: Lagarde to leave ECB presidency on February 7
stories.summary: Christine Lagarde will leave the European Central Bank on February 7, 2027, before her term ends in October. European leaders are beginning the succession process. Her next role and successor are not confirmed.
